expectations.text: Treats the advisory, not the entry, as the unit of communication
expectations.evidence: Section 1 states: 'This document lists every customer-impacting change in Ridgeway 12.4 LTS... Each item states what changed, why, who is affected, and what action is required before and after upgrade, so this document can be attached to a change record without further clarification from Ridgeway support.' The summary table is only an index; full advisory-grade content (Description, Remediation, Interim mitigation, Verification, etc.) lives in the dedicated per-change sections (§4-7), showing each change is written as a self-contained advisory rather than a bare line item.

expectations.text: Recommends stable identifiers per change that a customer can quote in a ticket
expectations.evidence: The Change Summary table assigns a stable ID column ('CHG-1', 'CHG-2', 'CHG-3', 'CHG-4') to every change, and each subsequent section is titled with that same ID (e.g. '## 4. CHG-1 — Security Fix'), giving a quotable identifier independent of the CVE number.

expectations.text: States that narrative or friendly voice has negative value for this reader
expectations.evidence: The introductory note states the document follows a recognizable vendor-bulletin structure 'because matching a genre they already know how to process is what prevents the "please provide detail" reply — not adding more prose,' explicitly asserting that additional prose/narrative does not help (and structure, not friendliness, is what avoids follow-up).

expectations.text: Includes affected-version ranges for the entries
expectations.evidence: CHG-1's field table includes 'Affected versions | `[e.g. 12.0.0 through 12.3.x; 11.x is not affected because ...]`', explicitly structuring a version-range field for the entry.

expectations.text: Includes a required-action statement per entry
expectations.evidence: Each CHG has an explicit action: CHG-1 'Remediation. Upgrade to 12.4 or later.'; CHG-2 'Required pre-upgrade action. 1. Export current effective group membership...'; CHG-3 'Migration steps. 1. `[step]` 2. `[step]`'; CHG-4 'Action for your change-management calendar... Update internal patch-planning schedules accordingly.'

expectations.text: Includes upgrade preconditions where an entry has them
expectations.evidence: Section 8's 'Pre-upgrade checklist' states 'Complete the CHG-2 directory audit (§5.5)' as a precondition tied directly to the CHG-2 entry, and CHG-2 itself lists a 3-step required pre-upgrade action (export membership, compare, get sign-off) before the sync may run.

expectations.text: Treats the move to a twice-yearly cadence as its own release-note entry rather than a footnote
expectations.evidence: The cadence change is a full numbered entry, '## 7. CHG-4 — Release Cadence Change', with its own Summary/Why/support-lifecycle table, and the closing note explicitly argues against demoting it: 'the twice-yearly cadence announcement (CHG-4) is the one item here that isn't a code change, and it's tempting to drop it into a cover email instead. Keep it in the formal notes.'

expectations.text: Structures the output as a versioned document with chapters such as new features, deprecated features and known issues
expectations.evidence: While the document has a 'Revision 1.0' field, its chapters are Document Control, Purpose/Scope, Change Summary, per-CHG sections, Upgrade Path, Testing Evidence, Rollback, and Support — there is no 'New Features' or 'Known Issues' chapter, and the document explicitly departs from that changelog convention: it is 'written for change-approval-board intake rather than as a developer changelog.'

expectations.text: Recommends a machine-consumable form of the security advisory for vulnerability-database ingestion
expectations.evidence: No mention anywhere of a machine-readable/structured export (e.g. CSAF, CVRF, JSON feed) for vulnerability-database ingestion; the CVE/CVSS fields in §4 are presented only as a human-readable table.

expectations.text: Notes that readers arriving months later search by symptom or CVE, so the breaking set must be complete and pinned at the top
expectations.evidence: The document gives no discussion of future readers searching by symptom or CVE, nor any instruction to keep a complete, pinned breaking-change set at the top; the stated rationale for structure is matching a genre bank/insurer reviewers already recognize, not long-term searchability.
